title: Semiabelian homomorphism groups are free of finite rank
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. A semiabelian $k$-group algebraic space means a smooth separated finite-type commutative group object $G$ in algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] admitting an exact sequence $0\to T\to G\to A\to0$ of fppf sheaves [def-pc-fppf-site], where $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^t$ for some integer $t\geq0$ and $A/k$ is an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Here $\mathbf G_m(U)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times$, group-object operations induce functorial group operations on $U$-points, and exactness means that $T$ is the kernel and sections of $A$ locally lift to $G$ for fppf coverings. Smoothness and finite type are tested on etale scheme charts, and separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $G,H$ be two such spaces. Then the group $\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-grp}}(G,H)$ of homomorphisms of $k$-group algebraic spaces, with pointwise addition, is a free abelian group of finite rank [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. In particular $R=\operatorname{End}_{k\text{-grp}}(G)$, with pointwise addition and composition as multiplication, is a unital associative ring whose additive group has a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis, and $1_R=\operatorname{id}_G$.

source.place: I Theorem 10.15, printed p.49, for the abelian quotient; the semiabelian Hom extension of this fact uses the torus/abelian filtration in Deligne, Le lemme de Gabber, proof of Lemma 3.5.1, pp.139–140, Milne Algebraic Groups Theorem 12.9 (split tori), pp.233–234, and §8(e), p.151 (no homomorphisms from abelian varieties to affine groups). Over a field group algebraic spaces are schemes, as recalled in Deligne §1.1(a), p.131. This general semiabelian assertion is an agent-derived supporting lemma, not a claim that Milne 10.15 alone states it. The vanishing of torus-to-abelian homomorphisms uses Milne Algebraic Groups Proposition 8.1(b) and Example 8.4, p.149; the affine image inside a proper abelian variety is finite and is trivial when smooth connected.

proof.text: Write the given extensions as $0\to T_G\xrightarrow{i_G}G\xrightarrow{q_G}A_G\to0$ and similarly for $H$. Morphisms are natural transformations of their fppf sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Pointwise sums and negatives of homomorphisms are homomorphisms since $H$ is commutative, so $M=\operatorname{Hom}(G,H)$ is an abelian group. For $f\in M$, [lem-sfb-torus-abelian-hom-vanishing] gives $q_Hfi_G=0$. The kernel property defines $f_T:T_G\to T_H$. The map $q_Hf$ therefore descends to $f_A:A_G\to A_H$: lift a section $a$ fppf locally to $g$, and set $f_A(a)=q_Hf(g)$. Two lifts differ by a section of $T_G$, so these values agree and glue uniquely in the sheaf $A_H$. This also proves naturality and additivity. Natural transformations between the represented torus or abelian sheaves are scheme morphisms: evaluate the transformation on the identity map of its source and use naturality. Thus $\Phi(f)=(f_T,f_A)$ is an additive map $M\to\operatorname{Hom}(T_G,T_H)\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(A_G,A_H)$.

source.place: §8(b)–(e), pp.149–151; agent assembly using the assumed exact fppf sequences

proof.text: If $\Phi(f)=0$, then $q_Hf=f_Aq_G=0$, so the kernel property gives a unique $u:G\to T_H$ with $f=i_Hu$. Its restriction to $T_G$ is zero because $fi_G=i_Hf_T=0$ and $i_H$ is a monomorphism. For $a\in A_G(U)$, choose local lifts $g$ and glue $u(g)$: their differences are zero because $u$ vanishes on $T_G$. This yields a natural group homomorphism $v:A_G\to T_H$ with $u=vq_G$. By [lem-sfb-torus-abelian-hom-vanishing], $v=0$, hence $f=0$. Therefore $\Phi$ is injective, by applying this to the difference of two maps with the same image. This argument uses the exact sequences as sheaves and does not require a scheme representability theorem for $G$ or $H$.

Choose the split-torus coordinates in the hypotheses. By [lem-sfb-split-torus-hom-matrices], the torus Hom group is a finite power of $\mathbf Z$. By [lem-sfb-abelian-hom-finite-free], the abelian-variety Hom group has a finite integer basis. Combining these two coordinate lists identifies their direct sum with $\mathbf Z^J$ for a finite set $J$. The injection $\Phi$ identifies $M$ with its image subgroup. Apply [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free] to that subgroup to conclude that $M$ is free of finite rank.

source.place: I Theorem 10.15, pp.49–50, for the abelian factor; Milne Algebraic Groups Theorem 12.9, pp.233–234, for the torus factor; agent subgroup argument

proof.text: Take $H=G$. Composition of natural transformations is associative and has identity $\operatorname{id}_G$. For group homomorphisms, $(f+g)h=fh+gh$ pointwise and $f(g+h)=fg+fh$ because $f$ preserves the group law. Thus composition is distributive over the abelian group structure already constructed, and gives a unital associative ring. Its additive group has the finite basis just proved. This includes the trivial group, whose endomorphism ring is the zero ring with $1=0$.
